interest: American firms renew business in occupied Japan through powers of attorney, 1947–49.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs
overview: This file from the U.S. State Department central decimal files (decimal file 894.0492) documents the administrative, diplomatic, and legal procedures governing the admission and authentication of powers of attorney for use in Allied-occupied Japan between May 1947 and May 1949. The records begin with the May 1947 announcement, coordinated through the Far Eastern Commission and the State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee, of modified theater regulations by the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) permitting United Nations nationals to designate agents in Japan to secure the restitution of confiscated, blocked, or wrongfully transferred property. The file subsequently details private commercial inquiries and corporate filings, including efforts by veteran merchant Everett W. Frazar in autumn 1947 to obtain clearance for a limited power of attorney enabling his former Japanese employees to reopen the Tokyo office of Frazar Shokai, and the May 1949 transmission by the Libbey-Owens-Ford Glass Company of executed powers of attorney granting agency to Y. Yamamoto in Tokyo. Together, these documents trace the post-hostilities transition from strict military custodial control over prewar assets to the gradual resumption of transactional communications and private commercial representation under the auspices of SCAP’s Civilian Property Custodian and the Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan.
